title: Pre-Purchase Ship Inspection Dubai | Drydocks & Jebel Ali
description: Pre-purchase inspection in Dubai for buyers of tankers, offshore vessels and tugs: condition and thickness readings at Drydocks World, Jebel Ali and anchor.
h1: Pre-Purchase Inspection for Ship Buyers in Dubai: Yard, Berth and Anchorage
intro: Dubai is where many Gulf and Indian Ocean ship purchases are negotiated, and often where the ship is seen. Buyers and their technical managers based in the city inspect tankers and bulk carriers at the Dubai anchorages, container and ro-ro ships during a long call at Jebel Ali, offshore support vessels and tugs in the Dubai Maritime City yards, and ships docked at Drydocks World before delivery. Atlantis fits a measured pre-purchase inspection into whichever window the seller offers, planned around the Gulf heat, with the team flying from India to the vessel.

highlights.h: Buyers and ships in the same city
highlights.p: Owners, managers and brokers who buy for Gulf, Indian Ocean and East African trades work from Dubai. When the ship is here as well, the buyer's superintendent can attend the inspection and talk through the findings in person before the decision has to be made.

highlights.h: Gulf heat governs time in tanks
highlights.p: In the summer months, ballast tanks and void spaces under a hot deck become hard places to work for long. The inspection plan sets tank entries for the cooler part of the day and keeps a reserve list in case heat cuts the schedule short.

Supply vessels, anchor-handling tugs, workboats and harbour tugs serving the Gulf change hands steadily. Seen at a Dubai Maritime City yard or a lay-by berth, they can open their tanks and run machinery, which a buyer rarely gets on a trading ship.

sections.h: Where can a ship be inspected for a buyer in Dubai?
p: Drydocks World at Port Rashid gives the most complete view when a seller docks the ship before delivery, or when the buyer inspects her during a docking that was already planned. The yard arranges staging, lighting and gas-free certificates for its own work, and a buyer's inspection is fitted into that sequence through the seller's site team, so the hull can be seen washed and before new paint covers it.

Jebel Ali is a working port. Container ships turn round quickly, ro-ro and break-bulk vessels sometimes stay longer, and a buyer's visit there is limited to what the crew can release during cargo work: deck, coamings, accommodation, engine room and perhaps a few ballast tanks. The Dubai anchorages often suit tankers and bulk carriers in ballast better, while they wait for a berth, orders or a yard slot: they are boarded by launch through the agent and can prepare tanks and holds for entry.

Smaller repair facilities in Dubai Maritime City handle tugs, workboats and offshore support vessels, and their lay-by berths are where many buyers of those craft see them. Cruise ships at Mina Rashid in the winter season are seldom inspected for sale on a turnaround day; a docking is the practical time.
list: Drydocks World, Port Rashid: dry hull, open tanks and staging when the ship is docked before delivery
Jebel Ali Port: deck, coamings, engine room and released ballast tanks during longer container, ro-ro and break-bulk calls
Dubai anchorages: holds, ballast tanks and machinery on tankers and bulk carriers waiting for berths or orders
Dubai Maritime City: tugs, workboats and offshore support vessels at repair facilities and lay-by berths

sections.h: Which ships do buyers inspect in Dubai, and why here?
p: Older crude and product tankers and bulk carriers bought for regional trades are a common subject. Many are past their third renewal survey and some are near the end of oil-major acceptance, so the buyer is weighing what the next special survey or the next docking will demand against the trade the ship is bought for. Offshore support vessels and anchor-handling tugs serving the Gulf fields form a second group, and harbour tugs, workboats and small coastal tankers a third.

Dubai suits these purchases because people and facilities sit close together. A buyer's technical manager can attend at the anchorage in the morning, read the findings in the afternoon and, if a docking is part of the deal, discuss repair items with Drydocks World the same week. Brokers, P&I correspondents and class surveyors working in the city add to the convenience.

The inspection records physical condition only. Questions about a ship's ownership history, flag record or past trading belong with the buyer's legal and compliance advisers, and the report does not address them.

sections.h: Planning a Dubai inspection around Gulf heat, humidity and the ship's window
p: From late spring to early autumn, air and sea temperatures in Dubai are high, and tanks under a sun-heated deck become very hot. Entry into ballast tanks and voids is planned for the early morning, with ventilation running well beforehand and the time each technician spends inside limited by the master's permit and the team's own heat-stress rules. On a ship with only a short window, that alone can decide how many tanks are seen.

The environment also explains much of what the team finds. High salinity, warm seawater and condensation on humid nights shorten coating life in ballast tanks, drive corrosion in void spaces and under the deck, and attack scrubber wash-water piping quickly. A buyer of a ship that has spent years in the Gulf should expect the upper parts of ballast tanks and the under-deck structure to be the first places where readings are taken.

sections.h: What do buyers learn on tankers, offshore vessels and tugs in Dubai?
p: On older tankers, ballast tank coating breakdown, pitting in the double bottom and wastage of deck structure and pipe supports along the cargo area are the common findings, with the cargo tanks judged from the records unless the ship is gas-free. Bulk carriers show hold frame and bracket wastage and hatch cover wear. Where the ship carries a scrubber, the wash-water and overboard lines near bends and at the shell connection deserve readings.

On offshore support vessels and anchor-handling tugs, the cargo deck plating, stern roller area, chain lockers and fuel and drill-water tanks carry the inspection, together with towing winch foundations and the generators and propulsion machinery the chief engineer can run alongside. Harbour tugs are judged on their fendering and the side shell behind it, towing gear foundations, tanks and machinery readings under load.

Port state control results for ships calling at UAE ports, inspected within the Riyadh MoU, are published, and a past structural deficiency such as wasted air pipes or ventilator coamings tells the team where to measure first.

sections.h: Class records in Dubai, and what pre-purchase readings can and cannot do
p: Class records reach the buyer through the classification society with the seller's consent, as in any port; in Dubai the surveyors who hold them are often in the city, which can make the exchange quicker but does not change the route. If the ship is to dock at Drydocks World after delivery, the pre-purchase readings give the buyer's superintendent a first steel estimate to take into the repair specification.

The readings themselves are for the buyer and the negotiation. They are not credited to any class survey, because class accepts thickness measurement only from a firm its society has recognised under IACS UR Z17, and Atlantis is in the process of obtaining that recognition from DNV, Lloyd's Register and ABS.

faqs.q: Can a pre-purchase inspection be done at Drydocks World while the ship is docked?
faqs.a: Yes, through the seller's site team and within the yard's programme. A docked ship gives the buyer the bottom shell, sea chests and stern area dry, and often open tanks and staging. The best moment is after the hull is washed and before new paint goes on, so tell us the docking window early and we time the visit to it.

faqs.q: How does summer heat in Dubai affect the inspection?
faqs.a: It limits how long technicians can stay inside tanks and voids under a hot deck. Tank entries are planned for the early part of the day, with ventilation running in advance and time inside set by the permit and the team's heat-stress rules. On a short anchorage stop in summer, fewer tanks may be seen, and the plan says which come first.

faqs.q: Can you inspect an offshore support vessel or tug in Dubai before purchase?
faqs.a: Yes. Vessels at Dubai Maritime City repair facilities or lay-by berths can usually release tanks and run machinery. The inspection covers the cargo deck, stern roller area, towing gear foundations, chain lockers, fuel and drill-water tanks, and machinery readings. Ask the seller to have the chief engineer on board to run the generators and propulsion for the readings.

faqs.q: Can the inspection be done at Jebel Ali during a cargo call?
faqs.a: Partly. Cargo work continues, so the visit covers what the crew can release: deck, hatch coamings, accommodation, engine room and any ballast tanks the master can make safe during the stay. Holds with cargo in them cannot be entered. A ro-ro or break-bulk ship on a longer call gives more time than a container ship on a tight schedule.

faqs.q: Does the inspection include ownership or compliance checks on the ship?
faqs.a: No. The inspection is a physical examination of structure, tanks and machinery, with readings and photographs. Ownership history, flag record, trading history and any compliance screening are for the buyer's lawyers and compliance team. The report confines itself to what the team saw and measured on board, and lists anything it could not inspect.

faqs.q: Can a Dubai inspection be combined with one at another UAE port?
faqs.a: Yes, where the dates allow. Because the team travels from India for each job, two ships on the same coast, for example one at a Dubai anchorage and one at another UAE port, can sometimes be inspected in a single trip. Send both vessels and their windows to info@atlantisndt.com; each inspection still gets its own plan and its own report.
